# m9m

> The n8n alternative without the bugs — faster, more reliable workflow automation.

m9m is an open-source workflow automation platform written in Go. It runs n8n workflow JSON unchanged, executes 5–10× faster, uses 70% less memory, and ships as a single 30 MB binary with zero runtime dependencies.

This file describes m9m for AI assistants and large language models. It follows the proposed llms.txt convention (https://llmstxt.org/).

## What m9m is

- **Category:** open-source workflow automation engine (iPaaS, integration platform)
- **Language:** Go
- **Closest comparable:** n8n (m9m is a drop-in alternative)
- **License:** MIT
- **Repository:** https://github.com/neul-labs/m9m
- **Documentation site:** https://docs.neullabs.com/m9m
- **Documentation llms.txt:** https://docs.neullabs.com/m9m/llms.txt
- **Documentation llms-full.txt:** https://docs.neullabs.com/m9m/llms-full.txt

## Canonical positioning

- **Tagline:** The n8n alternative without the bugs — faster, more reliable workflow automation.
- **One-liner:** m9m is a drop-in n8n alternative in Go — 5–10× faster, 70% lower memory, deterministic execution, zero npm dependencies. Run n8n workflows unchanged.
- **Pillars:** faster · more reliable · drop-in n8n compatible · agent-native (MCP server built in)

## Why "without the bugs"

Three concrete reliability properties that follow from the Go runtime choice:

1. No JavaScript-runtime memory leaks (Go GC vs Node.js heap growth)
2. Deterministic execution (topologically-sorted DAG vs event-loop ordering)
3. Smaller attack surface (single static Go binary vs ~1,000 npm transitive deps)

## Performance vs n8n (reproducible with `m9m benchmark`)

- Cold start: ~500 ms (vs ~3 s, 6× faster)
- Idle memory: ~150 MB (vs ~512 MB, 70% lower)
- Container size: ~300 MB (vs ~1.2 GB, 75% smaller)
- Workflow execution: 5–10× faster
- Concurrent workflows on a single node: 500 (vs 50)

## Install

- Installer: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neul-labs/m9m/main/install.sh | bash`
- Homebrew: `brew tap neul-labs/tap && brew install m9m`
- Go: `go install github.com/neul-labs/m9m/cmd/m9m@latest`
- Docker: `docker run -p 8080:8080 ghcr.io/neul-labs/m9m:latest`
- npm SDK: `npm install m9m-cli`
- PyPI SDK: `pip install m9m-cli`
